resolutions.researcher_notes: The existing ref was mis-flagged dead: the live arabnews.com page 403s, but its Wayback capture 200s and its body (fetched directly) confirms the 21 Feb 2021 Israel-Egypt ministerial agreement to build an offshore gas pipeline from Leviathan to Egyptian LNG plants. Offshore Technology independently confirms the same subsea gas pipeline plan naming Idku and Damietta. Two independent outlets agreeing the commodity is natural gas -> high/independent.

Both sources describe an offshore, cross-border pipeline moving gas from an upstream field directly to LNG export terminals -- consistent with 'transmission' -- but neither uses that literal classification word, so this is context-inferred rather than a stated label. Kept at medium/not-independent since the classification itself isn't independently stated twice, even though the underlying facts are.

Arab News (via Wayback; body read directly) quotes the Israeli minister's office: the two ministers agreed on an offshore gas pipeline from Leviathan to 'liquefaction facilities in Egypt' to boost exports to Europe -- matches the value almost verbatim except it doesn't name the two terminals. Offshore Technology independently names both Idku and Damietta as the LNG plants to be supplied, and World Oil corroborates the Leviathan-to-Egypt LNG framing. Three independent outlets -> high. The value's closing clause ('did not advance further') is the researcher's own status summary, not a claim any 2021-dated article could make -- it isn't separately sourced, only inferred from no pipeline having since been built.

Arab News datelines the agreement 21 February 2021 (Reuters byline, updated same day). Jerusalem Post independently reports the same El Molla-Steinitz meeting in Israel, dated February 2021. Two independent outlets on the same month/year -> high.

Arab News: the pipeline runs from Israel's offshore Leviathan field (StartCountryOrArea=Israel) to Egypt. Offshore Technology independently names the Egyptian end explicitly: 'Idku and Damietta' LNG plants. Two independent sources agreeing on both endpoints -> high. Beheira as the governorate for Idku is standard geography (Idku LNG plant sits in Beheira governorate) rather than a claim either article states outright, so it isn't separately corroborated -- flagged for the record, not a reason to hold the unit.
